items.title: Meeting highlights from the Committee for Veterinary Medicinal Products (CVMP) 14-16 July 2026
items.summary: CVMP opinions on veterinary medicinal products The Committee adopted a positive opinion for a marketing authorisation for Bexatil for the reduction of hyperglycaemia in cats…

items.title: Capricor soars on plan to amend DMD filing after adcomm setback
items.summary: Capricor Therapeutics has bounced back from a bruising FDA advisory committee meeting by securing a green light to file an amendment to its approval application, raising hopes that the biotech can rescue its Duchenne muscular dystrophy cell therapy. The biotech’s stock soared following the news.

items.title: PTC’s $211M bid wins Sangamo auction, teeing up ‘special opportunity’ to enter Fabry market
items.summary: PTC Therapeutics has struck a deal to buy Sangamo Therapeutics’ Fabry disease program for $111 million upfront, outbidding Astellas and TerSera Therapeutics for the near-approval gene therapy. Sangamo, selling assets as part of its bankruptcy proceedings, also offloaded technology to Eli Lilly for $50 million.

items.title: Zealand sells its rights to Takeda’s blood cancer drug for $100M ahead of FDA approval decision
items.summary: As the FDA mulls whether to approve Takeda and Protagonist Therapeutics’ rusfertide, Zealand Pharma has sold its own rights to the blood cancer drug in return for $100 million.

items.title: CytoDyn’s leronlimab reaffirms HIV potential after combo treatment eradicates virus in infant macaques
items.summary: CytoDyn's leronlimab may have struggled to secure approval as an HIV treatment, but research in infant primates has offered fresh hope for the CCR5-targeting antibody's ability to treat the virus.

items.title: It's BMS vs. Celgene investors once more after US appeals court revives lawsuit
items.summary: A U.S. appeals court has revived a lawsuit filed by Celgene shareholders that accuses Bristol Myers Squibb of slow-playing the approval of blood cancer drug Breyanzi to avoid paying out a more than $6 billion contingent value right.

items.title: BMS bags first FDA approval for CELMoD franchise with Zenbexus multiple myeloma nod
items.summary: In a historic breakthrough for targeted protein degradation, BMS has secured the first FDA approval for a CELMoD therapy with the clearance of Zenbexus (iberdomide), marking the first multiple myeloma approval driven directly by minimal residual disease as a surrogate endpoint.

items.title: Unapproved in US for decades, levosimendan stumbles in phase 3 as Tenax eyes narrow FDA path
items.summary: Nearly three decades after its failed bid for FDA approval, the cardiovascular drug levosimendan is still struggling to secure a decisive clinical win to enter the U.S. market.

items.title: Neurocrine stands by blockbuster hopeful Vykat XR as Prader-Willi docs raise potential safety flags
items.summary: Roughly a year and a half after the approval of Vykat XR, a group of clinicians with deep ties to the Prader-Willi syndrome (PWS) community is flagging potential safety concerns about the rare-disease med, acquired in Neurocrine’s $2.9 billion buyout of Soleno Therapeutics last spring.

items.title: MapLight dims preclinical programs to make phase 3-ready schizophrenia drug shine brighter
items.summary: Despite mixed results for its experimental schizophrenia treatment last month, MapLight Therapeutics is going all-in on the asset—at the expense of its preclinical programs.

items.title: PDS halts work on phase 3 cancer therapy to focus on colorectal contender
items.summary: PDS Biotechnology has called a halt to its phase 3 head and neck cancer therapy to channel resources to a drug in phase 2 development for metastatic colorectal cancer.

items.title: After tasting IPO success, Hemab’s CEO seeks ‘flavor of a multi-product coagulation company’
items.summary: With the post-IPO quiet period having come to an end, CEO Benny Sørensen, M.D., Ph.D., was free to sit down with Fierce to map out Hemab’s future.

items.title: Cullinan tees up J&J fight—and $100M payday—as Taiho-partnered drug hits phase 3 cancer goal
items.summary: Taiho Pharmaceutical and Cullinan Therapeutics have celebrated a second phase 3 victory for their small-molecule EGFR inhibitor, teeing up the partners to challenge Johnson & Johnson in a lung cancer niche.

items.title: AI clinical monitoring agent can deliver up to 82 times the ROI in oncology: report
items.summary: A new analysis from the Tufts Center for the Study of Drug Development (CSDD) found that an AI clinical monitoring agent can deliver an estimated 82-fold return on investment in phase 3 oncology trials.

items.title: After slimming down workforce, Aardvark scraps phase 3 trials as wait for next steps drags on
items.summary: Aardvark Therapeutics has confirmed it is walking away from recently terminated phase 3 trials, telling investors it has no plans to resume the studies “as previously designed” as it works to find a path forward for its stalled pipeline.

items.title: Samsung hearing aid features for its ear buds garner FDA clearance
items.summary: The FDA gave Samsung Electronics the go-ahead for the latest software features that allow its Galaxy Buds earphones to act as an OTC hearing aid that also allows users to diagnose their hearing.

items.title: Definium hits another phase 3 homerun with psychedelic ‘sea change’ for anxiety
items.summary: Definium Therapeutics’ LSD formula has gone two for two in its phase 3 program, notching a win in generalized anxiety disorder months after knocking a depression study out of the park.

items.title: Zydus’ Sentynl pens $475M deal for Mereo’s phase 3-ready rare genetic lung disease drug
items.summary: Sentynl Therapeutics has penned a deal potentially worth $475 million for the option to market Mereo BioPharma's phase 3-ready rare genetic respiratory disease drug in the U.S.

items.title: Fierce Pharma Asia—Legend’s first profit; Taiho, Cullinan’s EGFR win; WuXi AppTec’s reprieve
items.summary: As Legend Biotech became profitable, the company is navigating Carvykti's next phase of growth. Taiho and Cullinan's EGFR candidate delivered a phase 3 win. WuXi AppTec won a preliminary injunction against the Defense Department's black list designation. And more.

items.title: Fresenius pulls one batch of Actemra biosim over glass particle concerns
items.summary: Shortly after initiating a separate recall tied to mislabeled pain medicine, Fresenius Kabi is yanking a batch of another product in the U.S.

items.title: Regulatory tracker: Akeso's ivonescimab wins landmark first-line NSCLC nod in China
items.summary: In this tracker, Fierce Pharma is recording the regulatory progress of in-market products, including expansions into key geographies and new indications. Some of these updates may not meet the bar for standalone stories, but we think they are still worth mentioning.

items.title: ITM neuroendocrine tumor drug spurned by FDA over manufacturing qualms
items.summary: The FDA has denied ITM Isotopes Technologies’ lead pipeline candidate for a rare group of tumors due to qualms over the drug’s manufacturing.

items.title: AZ's blood pressure newcomer Baxfendy fails to meet cost-effectiveness bar, ICER says
items.summary: AstraZeneca’s newly approved blood pressure drug Baxfendy does not clear the bar for effectiveness relative to its price, according to U.S. drug price watchdog ICER.

items.title: Skye and Redx form new entity with $125M to advance fibrosis assets
items.summary: Skye Bioscience has entered into an agreement to combine with privately held fibrotic disease biotech Redx Pharma in a deal that will net $125 million in financing for the new public company, called Fibrx Therapeutics.

items.title: ‘We’re not afraid of competition’: BioCryst CEO sets out strategy after scrapping internal discovery
items.summary: BioCryst CEO Charlie Gayer told Fierce the company is “not getting away from science and R&D” despite shutting down its internal discovery efforts.

items.title: Chutes & Ladders—Former Legend CEO lands at K2
items.summary: Just weeks after Legend Biotech announced the departure of its CEO, Ying Huang, K2 Therapeutics has announced that Wang will now lead the startup, which was founded in 2024 with a $50 million seed round from MPM BioImpact.

items.title: Pfizer’s former chemistry whiz debuts Khartis Therapeutics with $95M for thyroid eye disease pill
items.summary: Three years after Robert Hoffman sold XinThera to Gilead, the veteran Pfizer chemist has unveiled his latest venture.

items.title: Medtronic veteran Bill Shields crosses over to become CEO at valve disease startup
items.summary: After 15 years with Medtronic’s structural heart franchise, Bill Shields is leaving the medtech giant to become the chief executive of startup Versa Vascular.

items.title: Fierce Biotech Fundraising Tracker '26: InduPro assembles $77M; Vaderis nets $152M series B
items.summary: The Fierce Biotech Fundraising Tracker records venture capital rounds of $50 million or more secured by biotechs.

items.title: Deerfield-backed Boulevard Bio embarks on ‘beautiful path to a cure’ with trio of immunology drugs
items.summary: Boulevard Bio has strolled out of stealth with $65 million in funding from Deerfield Management and three autoimmune disease candidates.

items.title: Amgen lays groundwork for new R&D center in Hyderabad
items.summary: Amgen is expanding its footprint in India with an R&D center in Hyderabad, the latest by from the California company to boost its research facilities.

items.title: Epicrispr raises $90M to rewrite treatment of rare muscle disease
items.summary: Epicrispr Biotechnologies has raised $90 million in a series C round backed by investors including Sanofi Ventures, positioning the biotech to advance a pipeline of epigenetic medicines led by an early-phase facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy prospect.

items.title: Fierce Biotech Layoff Tracker 2026: Aura loses 20% of staffers; aTyr shrinks by 60%
items.summary: As always, if you know of layoffs occurring at a biotech, please reach out to the Fierce Biotech editorial team.

items.title: Abbott teams with Google Health on AI-powered health insights app
items.summary: Two giants of their respective fields, Abbott and Google, are joining forces for a first-of-its-kind team-up that aims to build out a digital picture of people’s health.

items.title: Aura lays off 20% of workforce, rejigs C-suite amid R&D refocus on eye cancer
items.summary: Aura Biosciences is refocusing under its recently installed CEO, laying off 20% of its employees and overhauling its C-suite as it narrows its focus on ocular oncology.

items.title: Tavneos trial flagged for 'serious breaches' of protocol as EU regulators dissect market withdrawal decision
items.summary: With the European Union formally reversing its marketing authorization for the rare-disease med Tavneos last week, regulators in the bloc are laying out their concerns about the data backing the complement inhibitor in greater detail.

items.title: The Oral GLP-1 Tracker: Novo's Wegovy pill struggles to break through market share ceiling
items.summary: Fierce Pharma is launching the weekly Oral GLP-1 Tracker, leveraging analysts’ notes and IQVIA data to monitor prescription trends and shifting market shares as Novo Nordisk's Wegovy pill and Eli Lilly's Foundayo vie to become the go-to oral weight-loss solution for millions.

items.title: A genomics library for the AI era
items.summary: This week on "The Top Line," Fierce’s Fraiser Kansteiner sits down with Andy Deubler, chief business and administrative officer at Regeneron Genetics Center, to discuss the role RGC plays in the larger Regeneron model, as well as where the center could be headed as drug development pushes into new technological frontiers.
